gloss: Named surface set that implementers must provide
mechanism: A marker interface: a named set of surfaces a pattern requires of anything claiming it, so a caller can invoke across implementations without knowing which one it holds. A Trait has no instances of its own — it is claimed by other patterns, which supply the surfaces it names. Distinct from {{protocol}}, which is a Trait whose exchange must hold between two or more parties, and from {{contract}}, which is a signed agreement rather than a type claim.
invariants: Names the surfaces an implementer must provide, and which of them are mandatory.
Non-instantiable: a Trait is claimed by another pattern and has no standalone instance.
Says nothing about how the surfaces are implemented.
failure_modes: Claimed without provision: a pattern declares the Trait and omits a mandatory surface, so callers dispatch to something that cannot answer.
Surface set widened after adoption: adding a mandatory surface breaks every existing claimant, which is why the set is part of the Trait's identity.

surfaces.description: Surfaces an implementer must be able to answer.

mandatory.description: The subset without which a claim to this Trait is void. Solver's is Manifest and Execute of five.

claimants.description: Patterns declaring this Trait, where the library tracks them.
